routes.label: Add first, then take the reciprocal

question:
What is the value of the following expression?

\[ 10\cdot\left(\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{5}+\dfrac{1}{10}\right)^{-1} \]
solution:
First combine the fractions using denominator \(10\):
\[
\frac12+\frac15+\frac1{10}
=\frac5{10}+\frac2{10}+\frac1{10}
=\frac45.
\]
An exponent of \(-1\) means to take the reciprocal of a nonzero number. Since \(\frac45\ne0\), the expression equals
\[
10\left(\frac45\right)^{-1}
=10\cdot\frac54
=\frac{25}{2}.
\]
The answer is \(\frac{25}{2}\), choice C.
